subject: Re: Multi-year annualization plan + SLA credit — approval needed
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@greengrid.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greengrid.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Monica —

Great to meet on Wednesday. As discussed, GreenGrid is prepared to commit to a 2-year prepay for Redwood inference credits if we can get a commercial package that matches our ramp profile. High-level ask: 20% term discount off list pricing in exchange for a two-year prepay (year 1 lower, year 2 ramped). We need:

- A smoothing payment schedule (we’d like a 40/60 split Y1/Y2 with monthly recognition).
- An SLA credit if monthly availability falls below 99.9% (we typically ask for a 5–10% credit band).
- Net-45 invoicing on the prepay drawdown.

I’ve attached the SOW and an initial term sheet. Procurement is on copy for any legal/PO questions.

Can your team confirm if Redwood can do 20% on a two-year prepay and the SLA credit language? This is time-sensitive for our budgeting window.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships
GreenGrid Analytics

Attachments: GreenGrid_SOW_v3.pdf, Pricing_Term_Sheet.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@greengrid.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and for sharing the SOW. Quick internal note for Aditya and Marissa: GreenGrid is requesting a 2-year prepay with a 20% term discount and the SLA credit band. They prefer a 40/60 Y1/Y2 split (monthly recognition).

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Internal approval for a 20% term discount (we can structure the prepay as an upfront invoice with monthly recognition).
- Define SLA credit formula: suggest 10% monthly invoice credit for availability < 99.9% and escalating credits below 99.5%.
- Finance confirmation on net-45 for prepaid deals.

I’m pushing for 20% because GreenGrid is a strategic reference and has a fast product roadmap that could expand usage in 2027. If we can get internal sign-off, I’ll send a revised term sheet and DocuSign.

Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment (from customer): Pricing_Term_Sheet.xlsx

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Monica / Marissa —

Quick finance POV: 20% is higher than our standard for a two-year commitment given the volume profile they shared. We can consider it under the following constraints:

- Prepay split should be 60/40 (year 1 larger) rather than 40/60 to reduce collection risk.
- Require an MRR floor equivalent (minimum monthly consumption) to avoid downside if they underutilize credits.
- Net-45 is OK for invoice settlement, but prepay funds must clear before provisioning.
- SLA credit: agree to a limited-credit construct (cap credits at one month's average invoice per quarter) rather than open-ended.

If we accept 20%, I want the term sheet to include the MRR floor and the credit cap. Recommend approving 18% as a compromise if they push back on the floor.

Thanks,
Aditya
Revenue Ops & Finance (sales partnerships)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Aditya —

Understand finance caution. A few counterpoints:
- GreenGrid is an active reference in the edge analytics space and has committed to run a pilot with our dedicated serving path in Q1. That pipeline alone could yield 2x usage by end of year.
- The 40/60 split was their preference to align cashflow with their product ramp; I can propose a middle ground (55/45) if that helps.
- On the SLA cap: fair to cap credits, but keep the credit formula reasonable to avoid procurement pushback. Their procurement is fairly sticky on SLA language.

If Marissa approves on a conditional basis (finance sign-off + capped SLA credit + the 55/45 split), I’ll push the customer to sign this week. Timing hits our Q4 bookings if we close by 11/30.

Monica

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Monica —

I’m OK approving the 20% term discount with the following conditions:

1) Final payment schedule to be 55/45 Y1/Y2 (monthly recognition) to balance customer request and finance risk.
2) SLA credit allowed up to 10% of the monthly invoice, with a quarterly cap equal to one month’s average invoice (finance to verify cap mechanics).
3) Include a minimum monthly consumption floor (MRR floor) spelled out in the term sheet; if they fall below it, unused credits do not roll forward.
4) Legal to review SOW/SLA language; finance to confirm prepay timing (clearance before provisioning).

If finance/legal sign off, you have my approval to proceed with a 20% committed two-year prepay. Please circulate the revised term sheet and DocuSign link.

Marissa
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@greengrid.ai>, procurement@greengrid.ai
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year proposal — GreenGrid + Redwood

Elena —

Thanks — good news. We can approve a 20% term discount on a two-year prepaid plan, subject to the conditions below (Marissa has signed off pending finance/legal verification):

- Payment split: 55% Year 1 / 45% Year 2 (prepay invoice up front; monthly recognition).
- SLA credit: 10% of the monthly invoice for availability < 99.9%, with a quarterly cap equal to one average month’s invoice.
- MRR floor: minimum monthly consumption clause included; unused prepaid credits do not roll forward if floor not met.
- Finance needs to confirm prepay clearance before provisioning; legal will review SLA/SOW wording.

I’ve attached an updated term sheet (updated_term_sheet_v2.pdf) and produced a DocuSign envelope for the SOW and terms: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?d=GD-4712. Please review and, if acceptable, sign by 11/30 to hit our Q4 target.

Once signed, we’ll schedule a kickoff for provisioning and a joint success plan for Q1.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: updated_term_sheet_v2.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?d=GD-4712
